name: Biscoff Protein Cheesecake
description: Biscoff cookie-butter protein cheesecake, crustless. ~37 g Biscoff goes on top as an unbaked glaze (warmed, poured, self-leveled to a glossy mirror) with a graham-crumb rim; ~18 g is melted into the batter for an all-over biscoff note - never a baked surface swirl (that muddied the look before). The batter also carries a toasted speculoos spice blend (cinnamon + ginger + nutmeg) over the base's dairy ratio (light cream cheese 113 g + cottage 150 g + yogurt 150 g + egg white 33 g) for a dense, creamy set. Stabilizer setup: 2 tbsp AP flour + SF pudding mix (xanthan gum was tested in the flour's place and baked too gummy - reverted); the set itself comes from the eggs + whey. ~178 cal/slice, ratio ~11.9. To-make.

payload.instructionText: Finish with the Biscoff glaze: warm the 37 g topping Biscoff ~20-25 sec until smooth and pourable, pour it onto the center of the fully cooled cheesecake, and tilt the pan (or use an offset spatula) to self-level it into a smooth, glossy mirror over the whole top. While the glaze is still tacky, press a ring of graham crumbs around the top edge. Then fridge at least 4 hr - overnight is best and sets the glaze to a soft, fudgy layer. Best the next day.

payload.text: The cooked pumpkin must be at room temperature before it goes in - even slightly warm, it starts cooking the eggs and leaves scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth - any visible curd survives baking and turns the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works; a food processor needs a full 2 minutes.

Toast the ground cinnamon in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant before it goes in - straight from the jar it tastes flat; toasting blooms its oils and is what makes the spice read as speculoos against the Biscoff. Stir the ginger and nutmeg pinches in off the heat.
Don't overbeat once the eggs are in - mix on low just until smooth. Beating in air makes a lean cheesecake puff, then crack and sink, and it won't set to the dense texture this is tuned for.
A protein cheesecake sets firmer and dries out faster than a full-fat one - do NOT overbake. Pull at a just-set center with a slight wobble; chase a fully firm center and it bakes out rubbery.

Crustless by design - the Biscoff and toasted spices carry the cookie flavor without a crust's calories. If you want a crust, the Protein Graham Crust sub-recipe slots in like it does on the other cheesecakes (about +50 cal/slice).

Glaze only once the cheesecake is fully cooled - pour Biscoff onto a warm cake and it melts into the surface and slides off instead of setting as a clean mirror. Warm the spread just to pourable; over-melting makes it too thin to hold a layer, and it firms back up in the fridge.

Most of the Biscoff (37 g) goes on top as an unbaked glaze - undiluted and never baked, so it reads strong and stays glossy. A smaller 18 g is melted into the batter for an all-over biscoff note beneath the speculoos spice. Baking the spread as a surface swirl is what muddied the look before; mixed fully through the batter it just tints it and adds flavor, while the glossy top stays all topping.

Press the graham crumbs on while the glaze is still tacky, not after it sets, or they won't stick - a thin ring around just the rim frames the glossy top. For an on-theme version, use crushed Biscoff cookies instead of graham.

Warm the 18 g batter Biscoff 10-15 sec until loose and pourable before it goes in - cold, stiff spread leaves streaks, and since the batter is mixed gently (to keep the dense set) you can't beat the clumps out. The 37 g topping is melted separately, just before glazing.

payload.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 18 g batter Biscoff (warmed until loose), the toasted cinnamon (toast it in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant first), a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

Cool to room temp: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min (the gradual drop prevents surface cracks), then onto the counter ~1-1.5 hr until no longer warm (max 2 hr out). Don't move it to the fridge while still warm. Glaze it next, before the long chill.

Whisk the xanthan gum into the protein powder and Splenda while everything is still dry - NEVER straight into liquid, or it pearls into slime beads. Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, the protein-Splenda-xanthan blend, vanilla, lemon, the 18 g batter Biscoff (warmed until loose), the toasted cinnamon (toast it in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant first), a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg, and the vanilla pudding mix. Mix just until combined - don't overwork it; the batter will run noticeably thicker than before. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter firmly and longer than feels necessary - the xanthan-thickened batter traps air, and bubbles that don't escape bake in permanently.

payload.text: Xanthan (1/4 tsp) replaces the AP flour - the same water-management job at zero calories, and gum silks where starch dulls. It must be whisked into the protein powder + Splenda dry. The pudding mix stays: its gums carry the vanilla flavor and the proven track record. Escalation: if the bake reads slick/pudding-cup, halve the xanthan to 1/8 tsp next round before touching the pudding mix; if it reads bouncy, that's whey stacking with the gum - xanthan comes back out of this recipe.
Xanthan holds water, so the center wobble reads looser at the same internal temp - trust the 155-160F thermometer cue over your eye, or you'll chase firmness and overbake it.

payload.instructionText: Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 18 g batter Biscoff (warmed until loose), the toasted cinnamon (toast it in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant first), a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

payload.text: Xanthan gum was tested here (1/4 tsp replacing the AP flour) and taken back out: it baked too gummy. The SF pudding mix already brings gums, and xanthan stacked on top oversets the custard toward pudding-cup. The 2 tbsp AP flour is back as the water manager - starch dulls where gum slicks, and in a custard that softer set is the point. Don't re-add xanthan to this (or any pudding-mix) cheesecake batter.
